Yes, **R5 then R4 before R3** is the better order, and right now penguin has **0 free local slots** to launch any of them locally.

## Why R5 -> R4 -> R3 is better
- **R5 first (platform table + _platform()):** R5 creates the single `_platform()` helper and platform-rules table with a matrix test. Both R4 (computer vs web `real_project` rule) and R3 (matching step needs to platform profiles and `kit.py launch --web`) depend on platform rules—building R5 first avoids writing ad-hoc checks that R5 would immediately replace.
- **R4 second (local real-project check):** R4 removes a live bottleneck for every local part (`kit.py done` currently leaves `real_project` pending for the orchestrator even on a computer). Running R4 right after R5 also avoids merge conflicts in `scripts/kit.py` and the part templates.
- **R3 third (runner suggestions):** R1 (Antigravity web) and R2 (Gemini tasks, plus its 01:59Z concurrency addendum) both have their profiles ready, so R3 is not blocked on research, though R3 item 1 also references M9 (workflow on the map, still planned). Doing R5 -> R4 first gives R3 the clean platform table to plug into.

## Can I start one right now?
- **Locally on penguin: not yet (0 free slots).** `kit.py capacity` reports 4 running sessions and 1,280 MB free because 4 idle `claude bg-spare` processes are holding ~1,168 MB RAM (and M1's merge tests are currently running), so `.kit/device.py --gate` refuses a new local part right now.
- **Next:** Once M1 finishes landing and a slot opens (or on Claude Code web), I will start **R5** first, then **R4**, then **R3**.
